idiom_name: class with # private fields, readonly constructor params and branded ids
implementation_notes: The strongest boundary in TypeScript is the JavaScript runtime one: `#` private class fields (TS 3.8+ syntax) or the `private` modifier, which is only a compile-time check because types are erased. The root keeps `#lines` and `#totalCents`, exposes a copied `readonly OrderLine[]` through a getter, injects immutable collaborators via `readonly` constructor parameters, and brands its id type so aggregates cannot be confused. No ORM owns the unit of work, so a repository over the chosen client (Prisma/Kysely/TypeORM) plus one transaction per command stays application code.
pitfalls: `private`/`protected` are erased at runtime: an `as any` cast (or plain JS caller) reaches the field, so state the root must own has to be `#`.
A getter returning the internal array leaks mutation (and `readonly` is compile-time only) - copy on the way out when the value leaves the codebase.

TypeScript's structural typing lets an object literal satisfy an interface for the aggregate without passing through the constructor; validate at the edge and keep construction behind a factory or smart constructor.

Class fields follow `useDefineForClassFields` semantics: declarations without initializers are `undefined`, so either initialize in the constructor or satisfy `strictPropertyInitialization` explicitly.

variants.name: Functional immutable aggregate (data + pure update functions)
variants.idiom_name: readonly data shape + smart constructor + pure commands returning a new value
variants.implementation_notes: The same boundary expressed as data plus functions: a `Readonly` aggregate type whose parts are `readonly OrderLine[]`, a smart constructor (`createOrder`) that is the only way to produce a valid value, and pure command functions that validate and return a new aggregate through a `Result`. Choose this when the codebase is function-first (reducers, parsing at the edge with a schema library) - the invariant then lives in the constructor and in every command function rather than in a class, and persistence is still a repository plus transaction.
pitfalls: `readonly`/`Readonly<T>` are compile-time only and shallow: nested children stay mutable at runtime, so freeze or copy the parts when the value crosses a trust boundary.
Object spread copies the aggregate on every command; for large clusters this is allocation-heavy and each copy is a fresh concurrency version - keep aggregates small.

Nothing prevents a caller constructing the shape literally instead of via `createOrder`; enforce construction through the module boundary (non-exported type, factory exported) or validate at the parse edge.
Sharing the same `OrderLine` instances between old and new aggregate versions means a later mutation through one version is visible in the other.
